hook.line: After any surprise, the first question is always the same: what were you doing when it happened? Spanish answers with *estaba* plus the *-ando* form, then drops the event right into it.
hook.es: Estaba cerrando el café cuando se fue la luz.
hook.en: I was closing the café when the power went out.

examples.en: We were eating when Hernando arrived.
What were you doing when I called you? (to a friend)

examples.es: Estaba durmiendo cuando sonó el celular.
examples.en: I was sleeping when the phone rang.

examples.es: Alguien estaba haciendo ruido en la cocina.
examples.en: Someone was making noise in the kitchen.

examples.es: Estaba esperando el bus cuando empezó a llover.
examples.en: I was waiting for the bus when it started to rain.

rule:
You already say *estoy hablando* for right now. Put *estar* into the describing past and you get was doing:

*estaba*, *estabas*, *estaba*, *estábamos*, *estaban*
plus *cerrando*, *comiendo*, *haciendo*.

The *-ando* or *-iendo* part never changes; only *estaba* shows who.

It's the perfect frame for an interruption. The long action goes in *estaba ...ando*, the sudden one in the event past, joined by *cuando*: *Estaba durmiendo cuando sonó el celular*.

The plain describing past can do the same job: *Cerraba el café cuando se fue la luz* is fine too. *Estaba cerrando* just zooms in on the middle of it.

Keep the sudden part out of *estaba*. The phone didn't spend time ringing in your story; it rang: *sonó*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the past progressive: *estar* in the imperfect plus the gerund.

readAndPick.es: Estaba cocinando cuando sonó el teléfono.
options: I was cooking when the phone rang.
I cooked while the phone was ringing.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Estaba ___ cuando sonó el teléfono.* (*cocinando* or *cocinaba*) I was cooking when the phone rang.
yourTurn.answer: Estaba cocinando cuando sonó el teléfono.
yourTurn.why: After *estaba* comes the *-ando* form, like English -ing.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Estábamos comiendo cuando ___ Hernando.* (*llegó* or *estaba llegando*) We were eating when Hernando arrived.
yourTurn.why: His arrival is the sudden event: *llegó*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: What were you doing when I called you?
yourTurn.why: What you were in the middle of is *estabas haciendo*; the call is the event, *llamé*.

yourTurn.prompt: Someone was making noise in the kitchen.
yourTurn.answer: Alguien estaba haciendo ruido en la cocina.

yourTurn.prompt: Move it into the past: *Estoy esperando el bus.*
Make it about they: *Estaba durmiendo cuando se fue la luz.*
yourTurn.answer: Estaban durmiendo cuando se fue la luz.
accept: Ellos estaban durmiendo cuando se fue la luz.
yourTurn.why: They were is *estaban*; the power cut stays the same.

pitfalls.wrong: Estaba cocinar cuando sonó el teléfono.
pitfalls.right: Estaba cocinando cuando sonó el teléfono.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *estaba*, use the *-ando* form, where English uses -ing.

pitfalls.wrong: Estaba cocinando cuando estaba sonando el teléfono.
pitfalls.right: Estaba cocinando cuando sonó el teléfono.
pitfalls.why: The interruption is a single moment, so it takes the event past: *sonó*.

pitfalls.wrong: Fui cocinando cuando sonó el teléfono.
pitfalls.right: Estaba cocinando cuando sonó el teléfono.
pitfalls.why: This was is *estar*, in the describing past: *estaba*.

personal: Think about yesterday at eight in the evening. Write what you were doing (*Estaba ...ando*) and something that happened while you were doing it.
